chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Abi Umayr from al-Husayn ibn Uthman from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him): In

a man said to another man, 'A thousand dirhams are due from you to me.' He said, 'No, but they are a deposit (wadiʿah).' Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) said: 'The word of the owner of the money is accepted with his oath.'
ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling when a debtor claims a debt is a deposit rather than a loan?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the principle of *al-qawl qawl al-maliki ma'a yaminih* (the owner's word prevails with his oath), resolving the dispute between a creditor claiming a debt and a debtor asserting it is a deposit. This ruling underscores the evidentiary weight of the oath (*yamin*) in Shia jurisprudence when the claimant possesses the initial right to the asset, reflecting the practical application of burden of proof in financial transactions.
